name: itsukis-chat-hub
description: Itsuki's Chat Hub - a Discord-style client served as plain static files from GitHub. The SITE NEEDS NO BUILD STEP: index.html fetches the stylesheets and js/loader.js loads the scripts listed in js/manifest.js, in that order, into one shared global scope. This package.json exists only so the test and migration tooling is reproducible, and - since v54.6 - so the handful of things that used to live in loose markdown files are kept somewhere that ships with the code. See "comments".

comments.no-build-step: Visitors load index.html, which fetches css/ and js/ directly. Do not introduce a bundler, a framework or an install step for ordinary visitors. dist/index.single.html is an OPTIONAL one-file copy of the same app, produced by `npm run build:single`; it is a build OUTPUT, never the source.
comments.load-order: js/manifest.js is the one list of what loads and in what order. index.html carries its own copy of the CSS list (it has to - the stylesheets come from the raw repo and browsers refuse to apply them through <link>); the two MUST stay identical. Adding a file means adding it to BOTH.
comments.deploy:
Order matters.
1. ROTATE THE TWO EXPOSED CREDENTIALS if that has not been done. Both were once served in js/core/config.js and in dist/index.single.html, so they are in the GitHub history and are compromised; removing them from the code does not un-publish them. (a) Nyckel: delete the old client in the Nyckel dashboard, create a new one, and set NYCKEL_CLIENT_ID / NYCKEL_CLIENT_SECRET / NYCKEL_FUNCTION_ID as Vercel environment variables. The client id is not a secret and may also go in js/core/config.js; the SECRET never goes back into any file the browser is served. (b) Discord: delete the old webhook, create a new one, set DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL in Vercel. Confirm with `node test/security/no-secrets.js`.
2. Run the suites: `npm test` (offline) and `npm run test:browser` (needs Chrome).
3. Stamp the build: `BUILD_SECRET=<same value as in Vercel> node tools/stamp-build.js`, then set MIN_BUILD in Vercel to the label it prints. This is what kills every older open tab.
4. Rebuild the single file: `npm run build:single`.
5. Push the site files to GitHub.
6. PUBLISH THE DATABASE RULES - see "rules" below.
7. Deploy the api/ folder to Vercel if it is not already there. GitHub can only serve static files; api/ is server code (TOS logging, IP bans, the spin, NSFW scanning, username login). The site calls it over the internet, so hosting the pages from GitHub is not a problem.
comments.rules:
v54.6 CHANGES THE DATABASE RULES AND THEY MUST BE PUBLISHED, or server deletion by a site owner will fail halfway: the client sends one atomic multi-path write, and a single refused path takes the whole delete down with it.
WHAT TO PUBLISH: the contents of firebase-rules.json, into Firebase console -> Realtime Database -> Rules -> Publish. firebase-rules.min.json is the same document minified (some consoles reject the pretty-printed size); the two MUST parse to identical objects - test/security/rules-audit.js fails the build if they drift. Regenerate with `npm run rules:minify`.
WHAT v54.6 CHANGED: scripts/add_rules_owner_delete.py restores the site owner's branch-level DELETE grant on servers, serverChannels, serverRoles, serverMembers, serverBans, serverMutes, serverIpBans, invites, serverEvents, serverEmoji, memberScreen and roomMembers. Every one of those grants is delete-only (!newData.exists()), so it is the power to remove a server, not to rewrite anybody's data; the attack suite checks exactly that distinction. Nothing else was loosened.
ROLLBACK: firebase-rules.v54-original.json is a byte-for-byte copy of the rules v54 shipped. Keep it somewhere you can find in thirty seconds. Rules are not data - publishing them cannot change, move or delete a single record, and the worst case is an operation being refused.
rules-copy.html is a generated page that holds both copies for pasting; rebuild it with `python3 scripts/build_rules_copy.py`.
comments.setup: Optional subsystems, each off until you configure it. FILE UPLOADS: Firebase Storage rules plus the `files` rule in the database rules; with no Blaze plan, fill in the Cloudinary fields in js/core/config.js instead and uploads go there. VOICE: Agora - set CFG.APP_ID and CFG.TOKEN_URL in js/core/config.js; with no token endpoint the project must have its App Certificate disabled. CUSTOM ROLES: customroles/ is world-readable and .write:false for every client on purpose, so roles are granted from the Firebase console or through api/totmilestone.js - never from the browser. MVP/VIP GRANTS: need the MVP rules published or the write is refused. NSFW SCANNING: needs api/nsfw.js deployed and the Nyckel environment variables set. TRICK-OR-TREAT: the rules allow only the one rate-limited write shape; awards go through api/totaward.js, which is idempotent.
comments.security: Accepted risks are listed, each with its reasoning, at the end of test/security/attack-suite.js, and the suite prints them on every run. They SUCCEED BY DESIGN - a run reporting them is not a run that failed. The headline ones: the spin and several other economies are scored in the browser, because moving them server-side would break accounts that already exist; the real fix is server-side scoring. NEVER put a secret in js/, css/, index.html or dist/ - `node test/security/no-secrets.js` fails the build if one reappears. Site ownership is read from owners/$id and secretowner/$id in the database and from nowhere else: not a username, not localStorage, not a profile field, not a self-assigned role. Both the client and the rules test those same two nodes.
comments.testing: `npm test` runs the ten offline suites (rules, attack, compat, spin, migration) and needs targaryen: `npm install`. `npm run test:browser` runs the real-browser suites and needs Chrome. WHAT IS NOT EXECUTED BY EITHER: the Firebase emulator, and the Vercel endpoints over HTTP. targaryen is an independent implementation of the rules language, NOT Google's evaluator, so a rules suite passing is strong evidence and not a guarantee - publish the rules and try the real thing too. Treating the offline summary as complete coverage is the mistake the zero-case compat-diff once made.
comments.migrations: All optional, all additive, none required for v54.6. PRIVACY: scripts/migrate_privacy.js moves real email addresses out of users/ into userPrivate/; verify with scripts/verify_privacy.js; DO NOT use --clear-source or --rollback without reading the EXIT CODES table at the top of scripts/rollback.js first. AVATARS: scripts/add_rules_avatars.py then scripts/migrate_avatars.js move inline avatars to avatars/$id - a sign-in used to download about 18 MB because they were stored inline. Back up first: the JSON export is the only way back. scripts/estimate_quota.js sizes it before you commit to it.
comments.history: v54.4 gave site owners the power to delete any server and fixed the nine side-node paths the delete had always been refused on. v54.5 took the site-owner grant away again, keeping the path fixes. v54.6 RESTORES IT, in the client, in the rules and - new - in the server menu, which had never offered the entry even when the model allowed it. v54.6 also stops Discover reading a member count that was copied into the listing the day the server was published and never updated; the count is now derived live from the real membership records. v54.5's other work is unchanged: site-owner role resolution, the profile-card fixes, DM message requests, boost stacking, per-server moderation.
comments.v546-notes: Three things worth knowing before changing this release. (1) DModel.basePerms() answers 'what can this person DO' and folds site ownership in; DModel.storedPerms() answers 'what do their real role assignments grant' and deliberately does not. Only storedPerms is written to serverMembers/$sid/$uid/p, because that cache would otherwise outlive the ownership that justified it. (2) DModel.holdServer()/holdServerReady() temporarily attach a server the viewer has not joined, for a site owner managing somebody else's; nothing holds one by default, so ordinary members pay nothing. (3) Discover's counts come from per-server serverMembers listeners held only while the pane is open.
comments.markdown: v54.6 removed every .md file from the project on purpose. Anything that was worth keeping is in this "comments" object, in the header comment of the script it describes, or in the code it documents. Please do not reintroduce loose documentation files - put the explanation next to the thing it explains.
comments.targaryen: An implementation of the Realtime Database rules language, used by the rules suites. It is NOT Google's evaluator - see SECURITY-TEST-RESULTS.md. Pinned to a major version because the API differs between 3.x and 4.x: 3.x takes database(rules, data, now).as({uid}), and update() takes `now` as its THIRD argument while write() takes it as its FOURTH. Getting that wrong makes clock comparisons silently fail.
comments.playwright: Drives real Chrome for the browser suites. Only test/run-*.js need it; every test/security/*.js suite runs without it.
comments.no-dependencies: The site has no runtime dependencies. Firebase is loaded from the CDN by js/loader.js, exactly as before - nothing here changes how the site loads or is hosted.
